name: Production/Operations Web App
summary: A full-stack production tracking dashboard for PGM, a precious-metals recycling subsidiary under Elemental North America, built to replace spreadsheet/manual tracking with a real multi-user system
fullDescription: pgmproduction.biz is a live data dashboard, backed by an actual database rather than local storage. It tracks a lot (a batch of material) through its entire lifecycle: Intake, cutting, milling, lab analysis, pricing, shipping, and archiving with role-based permissions so admins and regular staff see different levels of access per module.
~9,600 lines of code, 41 API endpoints, 24 backend business-logic modules, and a 111-test automated suite
responsibilities: Lab/XRF module computing estimated returned troy ounces from raw sensor readings, and a Market Pricing module computing gross value, refining/treatment deductions, and net value per lot
Per-customer contract pricing (refining rates, treatment rates)
Shipping with two workflows, auto-generating print-ready Bill of Lading, packing list, and label documents for warehouse staff.
A searchable, filterable Archive of everything already shipped.
Employee Resources: an admin-managed document library backed by Azure Blob Storage.
QR code generation/scanning for physical lot tracking on the floor.

name: Mauri Foto Booking Site
summary: A photography portfolio and booking website for photographer Mauricio Gonzalez, styled to feel like an Instagram profile. It's a fully static site with no backend server or database, everything from photo galleries to booking availability is managed through a built-in admin panel that saves directly to the site's own GitHub repository. I built the whole thing as a single self-contained HTML file and deployed it on GitHub Pages.
fullDescription: I laid the site out as an Instagram-style profile page: an avatar, username, bio, and quick-action buttons for texting, emailing, and jumping to Instagram, followed by a payment methods row (Zelle, Venmo, and Cashapp, each with its own icon, handle, and a scannable QR code for Zelle) and a three-tab navigation bar for Portfolio, Packages, and Book, so the page never feels like one long scroll.

The Book tab is a full month-by-month calendar, styled after the native iOS Calendar app, that visitors can browse from the current month all the way out to 2037. Days Mauricio hasn't marked available are automatically greyed out and unclickable. Picking an open day surfaces the specific times he's offered, and submitting a request sends a pre-filled email straight to him with all the details.

name: Before We Expire®
summary: A fashion label with roots in the beautiful desert oasis that is Austin, Texas. Founded by Myself and Creative Vissionary Mark Mendoza
fullDescription: Before We Expire (BWE) reads like a warning whispered to yourself in a mirror. Two founders, one studio, working in that space between. It's a countdown somebody started and won't say out loud.

Some visions already crossed over into fabric, into something you can put your arms through. The rest are still on the other side of that glass, unfinished, watching, waiting to see if they get pulled through before the light goes out. You don't wear this because it looks good. You wear it because some part of you recognized itself in it before you understood why.
